input: s contains only ASCII 0 and 1 and has length L in [0, 4294967295], including empty input. Integers are plain int, excluding bool; lists and strings are ordinary list/str values, not subclasses. No concurrent mutation, getters or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Declared size bounds are not a guarantee of available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The number of nonempty contiguous substring occurrences containing equal numbers of zeroes and ones, with all zeroes consecutive and all ones consecutive within each substring. Thus each counted substring crosses exactly one boundary between two runs. Equal text at different positions counts separately. Empty input returns 0.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs, ordering and caller-owned containers remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state; separate calls share no mutable result state. Only previous/current run lengths and the count are retained; no substring copies or run array are allocated.
numeric: Run lengths are bounded by L. The sum of minima of adjacent run lengths is at most L-1 for nonempty input, because each minimum is no larger than its preceding run. The count and its final addition remain exact safe integers; empty input avoids negative length interpretation.
complexity: O(L + 1) time and O(1) auxiliary space. On each run change, add the minimum of the two completed run lengths; after scanning, add the last adjacent pair. No quadratic substring enumeration is used.
source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 491 UTF-8 bytes, including all 0 declared helper definitions/statements, their calls, the Solution/method wrappers, built-in operations, allocations, annotations/comments where present, whitespace and terminal newline.
